# Collapse and disclosure chevrons Opening or closing a group animates its height through grid rows (1fr to 0fr, never `height`) with a fade, and its arrow turns with it. The inner padding and negative margin keep focus rings of edge items from being clipped. Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes. ## Files | File | What it is | |---|---| | `collapse.css` | The `.sw-collapse` grid-rows animation, verbatim, plus the chevron rotation rules the app writes as Tailwind classes (`.sw-chevron*` are the CSS equivalents). | | `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. | | `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). | | `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). | ## Where the app uses it - `components/ui/Collapse.tsx` (used by `components/shell/SidebarSection.tsx` "More" and `components/shell/Disclosure.tsx`). - Chevrons: `SidebarSection.tsx` (180 deg), `components/ui/CollapsibleSection.tsx` and `components/card-designer/InspectorSection.tsx` (90 deg), `features/hub/landing/FaqSection.tsx` (plus to 45 deg), `features/docs/docs.css` (`sw-doc-nav-chevron`). ## Why Opening a group keeps its neighbours in view and shows what moved; the turning arrow reports the state before the content finishes moving. Closing is faster than opening. ## Timing, easing and distance | Part | Value | |---|---| | Open | grid rows 0fr to 1fr and opacity, `--sw-dur-base` 180 ms, `--sw-ease-standard` | | Close | to 0fr and opacity 0, `--sw-dur-fast` 120 ms, `--sw-ease-exit`, `forwards` | | Chevrons | `transform` 180 ms (sidebar, sections), 200 ms (FAQ plus), 160 ms (docs nav) | ## Trigger The `open` prop or `aria-expanded toggles `data-state="open|closed"`; `usePresence` keeps the region mounted for the 120 ms exit and makes it inert, so collapsed content is never reachable by Tab. ## Reduced motion The collapse animation is inside `no-preference`, so the region opens and closes at once; chevrons jump to their final angle. ## Dark theme None: colour-neutral. ## Do and don't - Do animate grid rows (1fr to 0fr), not `height`. - Do keep `aria-controls` pointing at a wrapper that always exists. - Do make closed content unreachable (unmount, or `inert` while closing). - Do not stagger children of an opening group. ## Copy-paste usage ```html

# Feedback: stamp, result, confetti How the product confirms something worked. A valid card check lands with one stamp; a result panel arrives with a small scale-in; a pass tears in from above; the workshop logbook opens like a cover; a completed return fires one confetti burst (only with interface effects on). Errors do not bounce or shake: they appear. Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes. ## Files | File | What it is | |---|---| | `feedback.css` | `sw-verify-stamp` (card verify), `sw-confetti-*` (return burst), `sw-result-arrive`, `sw-pass-tear`, `sw-logbook-open`, copied unchanged. | | `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. | | `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). | | `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). | ## Where the app uses it - Stamp: `features/cards/CardVerifyPage.tsx`, `cardVerify.css` (valid card check). - Confetti: `components/delight/ReturnConfetti.tsx` inside `SuccessCard.tsx` after a return is confirmed. - Result, pass, logbook: `components/delight/delight.css` on `ResultPanel` / `PassState.tsx` / `WorkshopLogbook.tsx`. - The primary success feedback everywhere else is a status toast (see toast). ## Why A confirmed result should feel confirmed, once, without delaying anyone. The stamp echoes a physical handover; the confetti is a rare celebration of a completed return. None of it carries information the text does not already carry. ## Timing, easing and distance | Animation | Duration | Easing | |---|---|---| | `sw-verify-stamp` | 420 ms, once | `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)`; scale 1.35 to 0.96 to 1, rotate -8 deg to 1 deg to 0 | | `sw-confetti-burst` | 1100 ms, per piece delay 0, 30, 60, 90 ms | `cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.3,1)`; 16 pieces in a fixed fan | | `sw-result-arrive` | 360 ms | `ease-out`; scale .96 to 1 | | `sw-pass-tear` | 360 ms | `ease-out`; translateY -8 px to 0 | | `sw-logbook-open` | 360 ms | `ease-out`; rotateY -8 deg to 0 (perspective 600 px) | ## Trigger Mount of the result. Confetti is gated: interface effects on, motion allowed, and never on kiosk, scanner, checkout or payment paths. The stamp is also gated by effects on. ## Reduced motion Everything is off: the stamp is inside `no-preference`, the delight classes set `animation: none`, confetti is `display: none`. The text and colour of the result carry the meaning. ## Dark theme Confetti colours are brand tokens (`--color-accent`, `--color-emphasis`, `--color-success`, `--color-warn`, `--color-info`); on a citron or yellow panel two of them swap for the panel's ink so pieces never vanish. The stamp follows the result colours. ## Do and don't - Do keep it once and under half a second (the burst is the one longer piece). - Do make it decorative and `aria-hidden`. - Do not use confetti in staff, kiosk, scanner, checkout or payment flows. - Do not animate validation errors (they appear, they do not bounce). - Do not add sound. ## Copy-paste usage ```html Verified

``` Confetti: `demo.html` builds the 16 pieces (`.sw-confetti-piece` with `--dx`, `--dy`, `--spin`, `--piece`) exactly as `ReturnConfetti.tsx` does. Cards, rows, tabs and links follow the colour-only rule. The Space Works mark's box-open is the one deliberate exception (see box-open). # Kiosk and display screens The rules for screens that stay on all day: the space display (a rotating slide show on a Raspberry Pi), the kiosk and the stats TV. Slides change with one opacity fade; the distance tokens are zeroed so every shared animation (route, dialog, drawer, menu, toast) becomes a fade. Nothing loops and nothing keeps repainting while idle. Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes. ## Files | File | What it is | |---|---| | `kiosk-display.css` | `sw-display-fade` (400 ms slide fade) and the `.sw-kiosk, .sw-tv` token override, verbatim. | | `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. | | `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). | | `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). | ## Where the app uses it - Display slide fade: `features/spaceDisplay/display.css` (`.sw-display-fade` on each slide in the space display). - Kiosk and TV: `.sw-kiosk` (`components/layouts/KioskLayout.tsx`) and `.sw-tv` (`features/stats/PublicStatsTvPage.tsx`) zero `--sw-enter-y`, `--sw-pop-scale`, `--sw-pop-offset`, `--sw-slide-x` in `styles/motionTokens.css`. ## Why A small Raspberry Pi browser, a wall TV or a shared kiosk must stay idle between changes and must never move content a bystander is reading. A fade shows a change without motion across the screen; zeroing the tokens gives every component that behaviour without per-component code. ## Timing, easing and distance | Part | Value | |---|---| | Slide fade | 400 ms `ease-out, opacity 0 to 1, `both` | | Tokens inside `.sw-kiosk` / `.sw-tv` | `--sw-enter-y: 0px`, `--sw-pop-scale: 1`, `--sw-pop-offset: 0px`, `--sw-slide-x: 0%` | ## Trigger A slide mounts or changes (key the element so the animation replays). # Overlays: dialog, drawer, sheet, menu, scrim One set of enter and exit animations for every layer that appears over the page: the scrim (fade), the dialog (pop), the phone bottom sheet (rise), side drawers (slide from their edge) and anchored menus and popovers (drop 4 px). Layers carry `data-state="open|closed"`; a presence hook keeps a layer mounted for its exit and makes it inert while it closes. Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes. ## Files | File | What it is | |---|---| | `overlays.css` | The `sw-fx-fade`, `sw-fx-pop`, `sw-fx-drawer`, `sw-fx-menu` rules and every keyframe, verbatim from the app. | | `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. | | `overlays.js` | Shared demo controller: waits for the actual exit animation, then opens the latest requested layer. Also used by the React demo. | | `react/OverlaysDemo.tsx` | A reusable React demo with the same frame, token skins and exclusive layer controller. | | `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). | | `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). | ## Where the app uses it - Fade (scrim): behind every dialog and drawer (`components/ui/Modal.tsx`, `DetailDrawer.tsx`, the docs drawer scrim in `features/docs/docs.css`). - Pop (dialog): `components/ui/Modal.tsx`, `components/layouts/FilterPopover.tsx`, `features/presence/PresenceCheckInSheet.tsx`. On phones (under 640 px) the same class becomes the bottom sheet (`sw-sheet-in/out`). - Drawer: `components/ui/DetailDrawer.tsx` (right edge), `components/shell/SidebarDrawer.tsx` and `features/docs/DocsLayout.tsx` (left edge, `data-edge="left"`). - Menu: `components/ui/OverflowMenu.tsx`, the user menu, popovers; `data-above` flips the 4 px offset when the menu opens upward. - Hook: `lib/motion/usePresence.ts` keeps the layer mounted until its exit finishes. Tooltips do not animate (they are native or instant). ## Why A layer that appears from just in front (dialog), from the edge it docks to (drawer, sheet) or from its trigger (menu) tells the person where it came from and where it goes when closed. Exits are shorter than entrances so closing never makes anyone wait. Focus lands on something that visibly appeared. ## Timing, easing and distance | Layer | In | Out | Distance | |---|---|---|---| | Fade (scrim) | `--sw-dur-base` 180 ms, standard | `--sw-dur-fast` 120 ms, exit | none | | Pop (dialog) | 180 ms, enter | 120 ms, exit | scale `--sw-pop-scale` 0.98 | | Sheet (phones) | 180 ms, enter | 120 ms, exit | translateY 2 x `--sw-enter-y` (16 px) | | Drawer | `--sw-dur-slow` 240 ms, enter | 180 ms, exit | translateX `--sw-slide-x` (100 %), mirrored for `data-edge="left"` | | Menu | 120 ms, enter | 120 ms, exit | translateY `--sw-pop-offset` 4 px | ## Trigger Set `data-state="open"` when the layer shows. To close, set `data-state="closed"`, make the layer inert, and remove it on `animationend` (or after the exit time plus 80 ms). Without animation support the layer unmounts at once. The complete demo uses one active layer and a pending request. Opening a dialog, sheet, either drawer or menu first closes the current layer; its exit finishes before the requested layer appears. Rapid requests replace the pending request. Escape and Close clear it. Reduced motion, including a preference change during an exit, finishes immediately. `sw-ov-frame` owns the containing block, paint boundary and stacking context. Its backdrop covers only that frame and never changes page scroll or layout. Panels use the panel, ink, line, focus and scrim tokens in both themes. The sheet has rounded top corners, a drag handle and safe-area footer padding; its body scrolls while the header and actions remain visible. Drawers fill the frame height. The menu is positioned from the Actions button and clamped inside the frame, including after resizing. Focus enters each layer without scrolling the page. Tab cycles inside a dialog, sheet or drawer; menu items support arrow keys, Home, End, Enter and Space. Escape, a scrim click or Close restores the opener. The handle is decorative; this template does not implement drag-to-dismiss. ## Reduced motion All of it sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; the app also zeroes every duration under reduced motion (`styles/motion.css`) and the JS hooks skip the exit wait, so layers unmount at once. The layer appears and disappears instantly; the information (it opened, it closed) is carried by focus and content. ## Dark theme Colour-neutral. The scrim and panel colours come from tokens (`--color-scrim`, `--color-panel`), so dark uses the black family and `--color-line` borders instead of shadows. ## Do and don't - Do give every layer a closed state and an exit. - Do make a closing layer inert so it cannot take focus. - Do keep exits shorter than entrances. - Do not unmount a layer instantly when animations are available. - Do not slide or scale on kiosk and TV screens (the tokens zero the distances; only the fade remains). - Do not animate layout properties. ## Copy-paste usage ```html

# React copies

`OverlaysDemo.tsx` is the kit's standalone React adapter. # Route transition

A page change reads as one move: only the main content region fades out (90 ms) and the new page fades in with a short rise, while the sidebar and top bar stay still. It uses the View Transitions API on the one named region and falls back to a CSS fade where the API is missing.

Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `route-transition.css` | The View Transition rules for the named main region, the CSS fallback (`.sw-route-enter`) and the direction distances, verbatim from the app. |
| `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. |
| `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). |
| `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). |

## Where the app uses it

- Every in-app link and navigation: `components/layouts/`, `components/shell/` (sidebar, bottom tabs, top bar), staff, member, public and docs pages. Only the element marked `data-sw-main` animates.
- Files: `lib/motion/TransitionLink.tsx`, `useTransitionNavigate.ts`, `routeTransition.ts`, `RouteTransitionGate.tsx`, `ScrollManager.tsx`, `styles/motionRoute.css`.

## Why

The visitor sees that the page changed without losing their place: the chrome is stable, the content is new. The old page leaves before the new one arrives, so the two are never visible together. Direction sets the settle distance (forward rises 8 px, a lateral move 6 px, back sinks 6 px, a fade-only change 0).

## Timing, easing and distance

| What | Value |
|---|---|
| Old page out | 90 ms, `--sw-ease-exit`, opacity only |
| New page in | `--sw-dur-slow` (240 ms), `--sw-ease-enter`, after 70 ms, opacity and translateY |
| Distance | `--sw-vt-y`: 8 px forward, 6 px lateral, -6 px back, 0 fade; kiosk and TV use 0 |
| Safety | the transition settles after 160 ms if the page is slow, and never blocks navigation |

## Trigger

A plain left-click on a `TransitionLink` or a push navigation through `useTransitionNavigate` sets `data-sw-vt="route"` and `data-sw-nav="forward|lateral|back|fade"` on `<html>` and calls `document.startViewTransition`. Back and forward buttons and unwrapped links replay `.sw-route-enter` instead.

## Reduced motion

No View Transition is started and `.sw-route-enter` is inside `no-preference`, so the new page simply appears. Scroll is restored instantly.

## Dark theme

Colour-neutral: the transition animates opacity and transform of whatever the page already paints, so nothing differs between themes.

## Do and don't

- Do mark one region `data-sw-main` and keep the sidebar and top bar outside it.
- Do keep the whole move under 240 ms plus the 70 ms offset.
- Do not animate the sidebar, the top bar or the browser chrome.
- Do not block navigation on the animation or wait for it before fetching.
- Do not slide or scale on kiosk and TV screens (fade only).

## Copy-paste usage

```js
const reduced = matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
function go(update) {
  if (!document.startViewTransition || reduced) return update();
  document.documentElement.dataset.swNav = "forward";   // forward | lateral | back | fade
  document.documentElement.dataset.swVt = "route";
  const t = document.startViewTransition(update);
  t.finished.finally(() => { delete document.documentElement.dataset.swVt; delete document.documentElement.dataset.swNav; });
}
```

Mark the region `<main data-sw-main>`. Without View Transitions, add the class `sw-route-enter` (and `data-sw-enter="forward"`) to it after swapping the content.

# Scroll reveal and pinned hero

The landing page's scroll story: the pinned hero sequence (copy lifts away, the real console rises, zooms through its surface and the overview settles in, all in one sticky scene), the handover steps beside a sticky record, and reveal-on-scroll blocks that arrive once. The default rules are the static page, which is what reduced motion, phones and browsers without JavaScript get.

Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `scroll-reveal.css` | The whole landing scroll stylesheet, verbatim (static page by default; pinned and reveal states only when the hooks mark the page). |
| `scroll-reveal.js` | Framework-free port of the hooks: `initReveal` (IntersectionObserver, once) and `initSequence` (smoothstep scroll mapping with the real ranges). The React originals are in `react/`. |
| `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. |
| `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). |
| `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). |

## Where the app uses it

- Pinned hero: `features/hub/landing/HeroSection.tsx`, `useScrollSequence.ts` (768 px and wider, when the copy, console and overview fit).
- Handover steps beside a sticky record: `HandoverScrolly.tsx` (1024 px wide and 640 px tall or more).
- Reveal on scroll: `data-reveal` blocks in `StorySections.tsx`, `AreasSection.tsx`, `FaqSection.tsx` and the rest of the landing page, via `useInView.ts‬ (`useRevealOnScroll`).
- Styles: `features/hub/landing/landing-scroll.css`.

## Why

Scrolling walks the visitor from the promise to the real console to the overview in one scene, so the product is understood by looking at it, not by reading about it. The handover record changes as each step reaches the middle, showing the evidence trail forming. Reveals pace a long page without hiding content.

## Timing, easing and distance

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| Pinned scene | 300 svh tall, scroll-driven transform and opacity (no timing), `will-change` only while moving |
| Ranges (fraction of the sequence) | copy lift 0 to 0.25, console rise 0 to 0.38 (smoothstep), zoom 0.55 to 0.84, figure fade 0.68 to 0.84, overview reveal 0.86 to 1; copy lifts 72 px, overview rises 32 px and scales 0.94 to 1 |
| Scrolly step | border and text colour 240 ms ease-out |
| Reveal | 640 ms `cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1)`, opacity and a 24 px rise, once, observed at the lower 12 % of the screen |

## Trigger

Scroll position (one passive listener, one paint per animation frame, geometry measured on resize); reveal on the first time an element's top crosses the lower eighth of the screen.

## Reduced motion

Static page, top to bottom in DOM order: no pinning, no reveal hiding, step transitions off. Content is never hidden from reduced-motion users, from phones or from no-JavaScript visitors. Print forces everything visible.

## Dark theme

Colours are tokens (`--color-bg`, `--color-surface`, `--color-panel`, `--color-line`, `--color-accent-ink`), so the story switches with `html.dark`; the console artwork has dark variants.

## Do and don't

- Do reveal once; never replay on scroll back up.
- Do animate only transform and opacity, and set `will-change` only while moving.
- Do keep the static page as the default and add motion only when it fits.
- Do not reveal on hover.
- Do not hide content from reduced-motion users.
- Do not read layout on every scroll event (measure on resize).

## Copy-paste usage

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="scroll-reveal.css"><script src="scroll-reveal.js"></script>
<main id="page"><section data-reveal>…</section><section data-reveal>…</section></main>
<script>SwScroll.initReveal(document.getElementById("page"));</script>
```

For the pinned hero, build the `data-seq` structure shown in `demo.html` and call `SwScroll.initSequence(root)`.

# Theme reveal

The Space Works light/dark switch animation. When someone presses the theme toggle, the new theme grows from the
toggle as a circle and covers the page in 720 ms, so the change reads as chosen, not as a flash. Where the browser
cannot do that it cross-fades; under reduced motion it switches instantly.

![Light to dark, then dark to light, as the circle grows from the toggle](previews/theme-reveal.webp)

Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser for the real thing (a page, a round toggle and a Light / Dark / System
picker). It uses the design tokens from [`../../tokens/tokens.css`](../../tokens/tokens.css).

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `theme-reveal.css` | The View Transition rules, the registered `--sw-reveal` property for the soft edge, and the cross-fade fallback. |
| `theme-reveal.js` | Framework-free classic script. Exposes `SwThemeReveal.switchTheme(next, originEl)` and `SwThemeReveal.applyTheme(next)`. |
| `demo.html` | Standalone sample page with a toggle and a segmented picker, including the no-flash pre-paint script. |
| `react/` | The SpaceWorks app's own files: `themeTransition.ts` and `themeTransition.css` (the reveal), `theme.ts` (preference, system, storage), `themeReveal.ts` (wrapper), `ThemeToggle.tsx` and `ThemeChoice.tsx`. See the import note below. |
| `previews/` | The animated preview (`theme-reveal.webp`, `.gif`), generated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`. |

## What it does

1. `switchTheme("dark", button)` finds the centre of `button`.
2. With View Transitions, the browser snapshots the old page, `html.dark` is toggled inside the transition callback,
   and the **new** snapshot is revealed through a circle that grows from the button's centre to the farthest page
   corner, **720 ms**, `cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1)`. The edge is soft (a 160 px feather) where a registered custom
   property can animate inside a mask; elsewhere it is a hard `clip-path` circle. The final frame is held
   (`fill: "forwards"`) so the old theme never flashes back.
3. The preference is stored in `localStorage` under `makerspace.theme` (`light`, `dark` or `system`), the
   `<meta name="theme-color">` becomes `#FFF4E8` (light) or `#000000` (dark), and `html.dark` is the single source of
   truth. Storage failing (a private window) never stops the theme from changing for the session.

## Timing and tokens

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| Reveal | 720 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1)`, grows from the toggle's centre |
| Soft edge | 160 px feather |
| Cross-fade fallback | 420 ms (class `sw-theme-fade` held for 460 ms) on `background-color`, `border-color`, `color`, `fill`, `stroke`, `box-shadow` |
| Colours | `tokens/tokens.css`: `html.dark` swaps every `--color-*` triplet; nothing else in the page changes |
| Browser chrome | `#FFF4E8` light, `#000000` dark |

The durations are deliberately longer than the 120 to 240 ms UI motion tokens: this is a page-level moment and never
blocks input (see `docs/motion.md`).

## Reduced motion and support

- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: the theme changes instantly, with no reveal and no fade.
- No `document.startViewTransition` (Firefox before 144, older browsers): every colour cross-fades for 420 ms.
- No `CSS.registerProperty` or mask support: hard-edged circle via `clip-path` instead of the soft edge.
- If the animation API throws, the theme is still applied. The reveal is decoration, never a dependency.

## Usage without a framework

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="theme-reveal.css">
<script src="boot.js"></script>   <!-- no-flash pre-paint script from docs/theming.md, synchronous, in <head> -->

<button id="theme" type="button" aria-label="Switch theme">...</button>

<script src="theme-reveal.js"></script>
<script>
  document.getElementById("theme").onclick = function (e) {
    var dark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark");
    SwThemeReveal.switchTheme(dark ? "light" : "dark", e.currentTarget);
  };
</script>
```

`switchTheme(next, originEl, options)`: `next` is `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"`; `originEl` is the element the circle
grows from (omit it and the circle starts at the top right). Options: `storageKey` (default `makerspace.theme`),
`onApply(isDark)`, called inside the transition when the theme is painted, for apps that mirror the theme somewhere
else (the design site sets `data-theme` there), and `apply(next)`, which replaces the default painting entirely (the
Theming demo on the design site re-themes one container instead of `<html>`).

**Pair it with the pre-paint script.** The reveal only animates a change after the page is up. On first load the
synchronous `boot.js` in `<head>` (see [`docs/theming.md`](../../docs/theming.md), section 3) must already have put
`dark` on `<html>`, or a returning dark-mode visitor sees a light flash before anything can animate.

## Usage in React

Copy `react/` into the app (the SpaceWorks app keeps them at `frontend/src/lib/` and `frontend/src/components/`):

```tsx
import { useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { currentTheme, subscribeTheme } from "./lib/theme";
import { transitionTheme } from "./lib/themeTransition"; // imports ./themeTransition.css itself

function ThemeToggle() {
  const theme = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeTheme, currentTheme);
  return <button type="button" onClick={e => transitionTheme(theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark", e.currentTarget)}>
    {theme === "dark" ? "Light" : "Dark"}
  </button>;
}
```

Call `initializeTheme()` from `theme.ts` once before `createRoot(...).render`.

### Import note for the `react/` copies

These are verbatim copies from the SpaceWorks app, so some imports point at app code that is not in this folder:

- `theme.ts` imports `./safeStorage` (`readStorage`, `writeStorage`: `localStorage` wrapped in `try/catch`). The plain
  `try/catch` versions in `docs/theming.md` section 4 are equivalent.
- `themeReveal.ts` is a thin wrapper kept for existing callers; new code can call `transitionTheme` directly.
- `ThemeToggle.tsx` and `ThemeChoice.tsx` use the app's `@lingui` translations, `useDelight`/`useReducedMotion`
  (`components/delight/DelightProvider`), `icons`, `ui/IconButton` and `ui/SegmentedControl`. Replace those with your
  own button and picker; the only theme-specific call is `transitionTheme`/`revealTheme`.
- `themeTransition.ts` also clears `data-sw-vt`, an app attribute a route transition uses. Drop that line if you
  have no route transitions.

## Source of truth

The SpaceWorks app (`frontend/src/lib/themeTransition.ts`, `themeTransition.css`, `lib/theme.ts`). `theme-reveal.js`
and `theme-reveal.css` are its framework-free mirror; change them together. `scripts/check-previews.mjs` fails when
`theme-reveal.css`, `theme-reveal.js` or `demo.html` change without the preview being regenerated
(`node scripts/make-previews.mjs theme-reveal`).

# Toast A status toast arrives from just below its slot (12 px, fading in) and leaves by dropping 8 px while fading. It never steals focus; the message is announced through a polite live region (errors through an alert region). Open [`demo.html`](demo.html) in a browser (it links `../../tokens/tokens.css`) and use "Toggle dark" to check both themes. ## Files | File | What it is | |---|---| | `toast.css` | The `sw-fx-toast` rule and its two keyframes, copied unchanged from `styles/motionOverlay.css`. | | `demo.html` | A standalone page with the live animation in light and dark, replayable. | | `react/` | Copies of the real app files (see `react/README.md` for the imports to replace). | | `previews/` | Animated WebP and GIF previews, light and dark (regenerated by `scripts/make-previews.mjs`). | ## Where the app uses it - `components/ui/ToastHost.tsx` (the one host mounted by the app shell): every save, undo, error and result message in staff, member and public flows. - `lib/motion/usePresence.ts` (`useExitingItems`) keeps a dismissed toast on screen, inert, while its exit plays. ## Why Status appears without taking focus or moving anything else, and its short exit confirms the dismissal. # Space Works motion kit

Part of Design System v2.0. Values are copied from the app as shipped in SpaceWorks 0.12.0.

Every animation in the product as a reusable, framework-free template: one folder per family, each with the CSS
(copied unchanged from the app, using the tokens in [`../tokens/tokens.css`](../tokens/tokens.css)), `react/` copies
of the real app files, a standalone `demo.html` (light and dark, honours reduced motion), animated `previews/`
(WebP and GIF) and a README that says what it is, where the app uses it, why, the timing and easing tokens, the
trigger, reduced-motion and dark behaviour, do and don't, and copy-paste usage.

The full catalogue with every trigger and reduced-motion note is [`../docs/motion.md`](../docs/motion.md). The
rules behind it: transform and opacity only, enter decelerates and exit accelerates, nothing on an interaction path
over 240 ms, hover is colour only, reduced motion is a floor, never loop outside a loader, check both themes.

## Folders

| Folder | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [`box-open/`](box-open/README.md) | The box loader (loop), the inline spinner, the in-button mono spinner, the logo hover and focus opening, the cold-start splash opening |
| [`theme-reveal/`](theme-reveal/README.md) | The light/dark switch: a circle growing from the toggle |
| [`search/`](search/README.md) | The shared animated search field |

| [`toast/`](toast/README.md) | Status toast in and out |
| [`sidebar/`](sidebar/README.md) | Sliding section and tab indicator |
